mechanism: ARM 1 of the original program (exp 38): budget-elasticity curve. One-constant changes of the certified field-floor vehicle (max_runtime_s_per_game 7920 -> 3960 / 23760), everything else byte-identical. Motivated by the panel headline: 675/675 recorded game-runs ended gave_up at the cap; 17 turns/game vs 132 designed; the decision budget hypothesized as the binding constraint and the common cause of the 0-for-6 additions sweep.
sealed_reading_rule: epsilon = dln(lc)/dln(budget) across three points; T1 = TWO replicates {28, 30} mean 29 (never a single run); trim1 screening primary, mean_score retired; bands: HIGH >=0.60 (lc(T3)>=45 AND lc(T05)<=22), KILL <0.25 (lc(T3)<=33), PARTIAL between, ANOMALY lc(T3)<24 with turns>=2x. Asymmetry guard bound pre-read: downward elasticity does not license upward expectations; PARTIAL goes to the coordinator with the turns proxy, never read as 'ship throughput'.

instrument_note: Taxonomy species #5, found against the real T0.5 artifact BEFORE the elasticity read: the solver banner echoes the PICKLED DEFAULT (7920.0), printed before the customization cell assigns - an echo captured before the treatment applies certifies nothing. why_informative: The campaign's first measured elasticity curve, and the shape answers the program's gating question with precision the single epsilon hides: the budget binds at slope ~1.05 BELOW our operating point and saturates to ~0.17 ABOVE it. The decision-budget thesis is confirmed as the binding constraint AT THE MARGIN yet nearly exhausted as an upside lever: naive 1.5x throughput projects ~+2 levels against the ~+16 the 2.5 tier requires. This prices the entire throughput family (C2/C3/C7) at the slope, hands C4 its promotion per the sealed band text, and does it for 7.9 GPU-h and zero submission slots. The asymmetry guard (sealed pre-read) is what kept the loud downward segment from being read as an upward promise - the guard did exactly its job.
